text:
Maya: Quick UX question — when the autoswitch policy flips to a degraded model, do we show the reason in Console or keep it opaque? customers keep asking why results changed.
Liam: leaning toward showing a compact reason: e.g. 'switched: error rate spike' + policy id. must avoid exposing internal thresholds though.
Sofia: +1. also include a link to the rollout/audit entry so SREs can inspect. Maybe a small toast: 'Autoswitched for tenant X — view details'. :eyes: 
Eva: We should show what degraded mode means for that tenant: whether it's quality degrade (smaller model), latency degrade (lower batch size), or hard failover (cached response). Otherwise product teams panic.
Maya: Good call. Proposal: Console shows three items: 1) short reason string, 2) degrade mode type, 3) link to audit record. Clicking audit shows full event.
Liam: For audit records, we need immutable fields: policy_id, trigger_metric (e.g. 5xx_rate), threshold, window, timestamp, decision (auto/manual), and who/what triggered it. Also we should attach a sampled request log (redacted) for debugging.
Sofia: We should also capture the fallback model details and the routing decision: e.g. target_model: redwood/gpt-medium-q4f. important for reproducing diffs.
Maya: UX question — should we surface the raw metric values? e.g. '5xx-rate 7.3% > threshold 5% over 2m'. Helpful but might scare non-technical PMs.
Liam: We can hide raw values behind an "advanced details" link. Default short text for product users, expanded for SRE/DevOps.
ops-bot: ALERT: autoswitch triggered (policy: autoswitch-main-3) tenant: acme-fin — trigger: 5xx_rate 7.3% window: 120s -> switched to model redwood/fast-quantized-1 :rotating_light:
Eva: Important policy edge-case: what if autoswitch oscillates? need a cooldown TTL and a circuit-breaker state to avoid flapping. This also affects what we show in Console (e.g. 'on cooldown until 2024-04-02T14:12Z').
Sofia: Agree. Also add a 'reason history' timeline in the audit detail: timestamps of each decision + brief note.
Maya: Security/PII note — if we store sampled request text, must redact PII and show that in the audit UI with a redaction badge. Add retention TTL (90 days?) and per-customer policy override.
Liam: On the API side, we should expose a stable audit endpoint: GET /v1/audit/policies/{policy_id}/events?tenant=... that returns event summaries. For full playback only accessible to admins.
Sofia: Example audit event (proposal):
```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01G...",
  "policy_id": "autoswitch-main-3",
  "tenant": "acme-fin",
  "trigger": "5xx_rate",
  "metric_value": "7.3",
  "threshold": "5.0",
  "window_s": "120",
  "decision": "auto_switch",
  "from_model": "redwood/paas-large",
  "to_model": "redwood/fast-quantized-1",
  "timestamp": "2024-04-02T14:03:09Z",
  "actor": "ops-bot"
}
```
Eva: Love it. For telemetry, we should emit a compact event into our tracing pipeline so metrics and alerts can correlate a model switch with downstream latencies. Add a tag for rollout.cause and examplar request id.
Maya: UX extra: allow teams to annotate audit events with a short note (e.g., "investigating infra flakiness") so later playback isn't just noise. Make annotations optional and access-controlled.
Liam: Action items: 1) frontend: add toast + audit detail mock (Sofia) 2) backend: audit schema + endpoint + retention (Liam) 3) infra: ensure sample redaction and tracing tags (Eva) 4) policy: cooldown default = 10m, sample rate = 1% for request payloads (Maya)
Sofia: I'll drop a mock into Figma by EOD and add a tiny inline copy suggestion for non-technical users.
Maya: I'll write the short API proposal and include fields we agreed on. Also will add a note about per-tenant overrides and GDPR opt-out.
DeployBot: deploy status: no changes yet. PRs referenced: none.
Liam: One more UX ask — provide a console control to 'mute notifications' for teams that only want audit but not toasty alerts. Keep it per-team and per-policy.
Maya: Sounds good. We'll iterate on wording. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
